To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

organizational resilience is a function of material resources, preparedness, information management, redundancy, governance, leadership, human capital, organizational culture, social networks and collaborative relationships.

resilience is the capacity of a health system to continue to perform and improve in the face of adversity, shocks, and stress, and to do this in ways that are sustainable and equitable, and that this capacity depends on a combination of factors including the system's preparedness, planning, governance, leadership, and the health system's culture, as well as its hardware and software.
organizational resilience is influenced by material resources, preparedness & planning, information management & communication, governance & leadership, organizational culture & social networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ability of health systems to adapt to, and transform from, shocks and stresses, and to do so in ways that are consistent with their objectives and that do not compromise their core functions.
the resilience of health organizations, not only to acute shocks, but also chronic stresses and routine disruptions.
the resilience of complex adaptive systems, which are composed of multiple interacting components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
resilience is a function of both hardware and software.

the resilience of an organization can be enhanced by: (i) investing in material resources, (ii) planning for and preparing to manage shocks and stresses, (iii) managing information, (iv) creating redundancy in the system and collateral pathways, (v) ensuring good governance and effective leadership, (vi) fostering an organizational culture that supports resilience, (vii) investing in the human capital of the workforce, (viii) building social networks and collaborations.

resilience is a complex concept that can be defined as the ability of an organization, system or community to absorb disturbance and re-organize while undergoing change so as to still retain essentially the same function, structure, or identity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the health system resilience literature can be used to guide the development of health system capacity to withstand shocks and to adapt to stresses.
resilience is a complex concept and it is important for health system actors to understand the concept and how it can be nurtured.
resilience is a system's capacity for self-organisation, learning and adaptation that enables it to deal with change and continue to develop.
The main takeaway from our work is that
health system resilience is an emergent property that can be nurtured through a combination of planned and adaptive approaches.
resilience is a complex concept and cannot be reduced to a simple formula.
health system resilience cannot be planned for in isolation, but must be nurtured through a combination of deliberate actions and the creation of enabling environments.
